title: Acts of Parliament and statutory instruments that change the money or operating terms of listed Kenyan companies, 2021 to 2026
basis: A map of statutory mechanisms, not legal advice and not investment advice. Each record is one Act or statutory instrument whose text changes a cost, a tax, a licence or a market term that reaches an issuer listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. It records what the instrument does mechanically, not whether it is good or bad, and not what any share price will do. Tickers are the issuers the mechanism can reach, not a claim that the mechanism currently binds that issuer. The sentinel ALL means every issuer in listing_NSE.json. Status is the legislative status of the instrument itself: enacted, amended, bill, withdrawn or repealed.

conventions.tickers_semantics: Issuers the mechanism can reach. ALL means every issuer in the listing file.
sources_accepted: Kenya Law Reports (kenyalaw.org) text of the Act, subsidiary legislation or judgment
Parliament of Kenya (parliament.go.ke) records and committee reports
conventions.dashes: No em dashes or en dashes are used in this file.
conventions.clauses: Every record names the exact provision that does the thing the mechanism describes. A clause was only written down after it was read in the Act's own text as published by Kenya Law, the same document the record's source cites, on 2026-11-13. Where an Act amends another statute the citation names both: the section of the amending Act, and the provision of the principal Act as it now reads. Where a figure is set by subsidiary legislation rather than by the Act, that is said instead of a regulation number being supplied. A record with no enacted text carries clauses_not_on_file with the reason, and never a guessed number.

sources.name: Kenya Law Reports (National Council for Law Reporting)
Parliament of Kenya, National Assembly Bills Tracker

laws.name: Finance Act, 2021 (No. 8 of 2021)
laws.status_note: In force; its amendments remain on the statute book unless later rewritten by a subsequent Finance Act.
laws.mechanism: Rewrites the interest deduction rule in section 16(2)(j) of the Income Tax Act so that gross interest paid to related persons and third parties above 30 per cent of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation is not deductible, with banks and licensed micro and small enterprises excluded.
other_mechanisms: Amends the Insurance Act to allow closed funds and to require insurers to pay a prescribed annual fee.
Adds excise duty on ring back tune sales by mobile telecommunication service providers.

source.name: Finance Act, 2021, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Deletes paragraph (j) of section 16(2) of the Income Tax Act and substitutes a new paragraph (j): gross interest paid or payable to related persons and third parties in excess of thirty per cent of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of the borrower in any financial year.
The deduction rule itself, in the principal Act, as it now reads.

laws.name: Finance Act, 2022 (No. 22 of 2022)
laws.status_note: In force; several rates it set were later changed by the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024 and by later Finance Acts.
laws.mechanism: Adds excise duty of 10 per cent of the excisable value on imported cellular phones, which is a landed cost for any listed company that imports handsets for sale.
other_mechanisms: Adds excise duty of 20 per cent on fees charged by digital lenders.
Zero rates fertilisers and the export of business process outsourcing services, and removes one exempt item from Part B of the Second Schedule.

source.name: Finance Act, 2022, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Inserts new paragraphs after paragraph 5 of Part II of the First Schedule to the Excise Duty Act: paragraph 6, excise duty on fees charged by digital lenders at twenty per cent, and paragraph 7, excise duty on the importation of cellular phones at ten per cent of the excisable value.
The cellular phone rate itself, in the principal Act.

laws.name: Finance Act, 2023 (No. 4 of 2023)
laws.status_note: The Supreme Court in Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury and Planning and 4 others v Okoiti and 52 others [2024] KESC 63 set aside the Court of Appeal finding that the whole Act was unconstitutional, upheld the striking out of sections 76, 78 and 87, and left the rest of the Act in force. The housing levy in section 84 was superseded by the Affordable Housing Act, 2024.
laws.mechanism: Inserts sections 31B and 31C into the Employment Act, 2007 so that every employee and every employer each pay a monthly Affordable Housing Levy of 1.5 per cent of the employee gross monthly salary, with the employer required to deduct and remit both shares within nine working days of the end of the month.
other_mechanisms: Increases the top PAYE rate and reduces the number of bands.
Changes VAT treatment of petroleum products and of several exempt goods.
Adds excise duty on betting and gaming amounts wagered.

source.name: Finance Act, 2023, Kenya Law Reports

source_court.name: Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury and Planning and 4 others v Okoiti and 52 others [2024] KESC 63

clauses.effect: Inserts new sections 31B and 31C immediately after section 31A of the Employment Act, 2007.
Each employee and employer shall pay a monthly levy to be known as the Affordable Housing Levy, notwithstanding section 3(2)(a) to (d) of that Act.
Obligations of the employer: deduction, the employer's own share, and remittance.

laws.name: Affordable Housing Act, 2024 (No. 2 of 2024)
laws.status_note: In force. It replaced the housing levy that had been introduced into the Employment Act by the Finance Act, 2023 and gives the levy its own statutory basis.
laws.mechanism: Imposes the Affordable Housing Levy at 1.5 per cent of an employee gross salary and requires the employer to remit an amount equal to the amount deducted, making the levy a standing payroll cost for every listed employer.
other_mechanisms: Creates the Affordable Housing Fund and the collector role for the levy.
Permits a commission of up to 2 per cent of collected monies to the collector, as amended by the Finance Act, 2026.

source.name: Affordable Housing Act, 2024, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: There is imposed a levy known as the Affordable Housing Levy.
The Levy shall be at the rate of one point five per cent of the gross salary of an employee.
Payable to the collector not later than the ninth working day after the end of the month.
The employer shall deduct and remit the employee's amount, and remit an amount equivalent to the amount deducted. That second limb is what makes the Levy an employer cost.

laws.name: Social Health Insurance Act, 2023 (No. 16 of 2023)
laws.status_note: In force. On 19 January 2024 the Court of Appeal suspended High Court orders that had restrained commencement of this Act, the Primary Health Care Act, 2023 and the Digital Health Act, 2023, leaving three sections of this Act suspended pending appeal.
laws.mechanism: Repeals the National Health Insurance Fund Act and makes contribution to the Social Health Insurance Fund a statutory monthly deduction from wages at 2.75 per cent of gross salary under the regulations gazetted under the Act, which the employer must deduct and remit.
other_mechanisms: Establishes the Social Health Authority and three funds.
Changes the statutory basis on which private medical cover sits alongside a public contributory scheme.

source.name: Social Health Insurance Act, 2023, Kenya Law Reports

source_court.name: Cabinet Secretary Ministry of Health v Aura and 13 others [2024] KECA 2

clauses.effect: Names who is liable to contribute to the Fund: every Kenyan household, a non-Kenyan resident ordinarily resident for more than twelve months, the national government, a county government and any other employer.

Where household income is derived from salaried employment, the contribution is paid by a monthly statutory deduction from the wages or salary by the employer AT A RATE PRESCRIBED UNDER THIS ACT. The Act itself fixes no percentage: the 2.75 per cent is set by regulations made under the Act, and the regulation that sets it is not on file here, so it is not cited as though the Act said it.

laws.name: Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024 (No. 12 of 2024)
laws.status_note: In force. Its excise rates were carried forward into the Excise Duty Act First Schedule and remain the reference rates unless changed by a later Finance Act.
laws.mechanism: Sets the excise rate on beer, cider, perry, mead, opaque beer and similar fermented beverages at KSh 22.50 per centilitre of pure alcohol, with a KSh 10 per centilitre rate for licensed small independent brewers producing no more than 150,000 litres a month, so the duty per unit of alcohol depends on the size of the brewer.
other_mechanisms: Raises the Railway Development Levy on imports from 1.5 per cent to 2 per cent of customs value.
Sets excise duty on imported sugar at KSh 7.50 per kilogram.
Replaces digital service tax with significant economic presence tax on non-resident digital sellers.
Changes the excise rate on cigarettes with filters.

source.name: Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: In the second table of paragraph 1 of Part I of the First Schedule to the Excise Duty Act, deletes the rate for beer, cider, perry, mead, opaque beer and mixtures of fermented beverages of alcoholic strength not exceeding 6 per cent and substitutes KSh 22.50 per centilitre of pure alcohol, with a proviso for small brewers.
The same rate of KSh 22.50 per centilitre of pure alcohol for wines, including fortified wines and other fermented fruit beverages.

laws.name: Tax Procedures (Amendment) Act, 2024 (No. 21 of 2024)
laws.status_note: In force; further amended by the Finance Act, 2025 and the Finance Act, 2026.
laws.mechanism: Prescribes the information an electronic tax invoice must carry before it can support a claim and rewrites the offset and refund provisions, so the cash a company can recover, and when, depends on invoice format and the statutory timelines.
other_mechanisms: Adds a relief mechanism where double taxation arises.
Amends objection and appeal procedures and penalties for late returns.

source.name: Tax Procedures (Amendment) Act, 2024, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Inserts section 23A(2A) into the Tax Procedures Act, listing what an electronic tax invoice must contain: the words TAX INVOICE, the name, address and PIN of the supplier, the name, address and PIN of the purchaser where there is one, the serial number, and the date and time of issue and of supply.
Amends section 6A of the Tax Procedures Act (Cap. 469B).

laws.name: Business Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024 (No. 20 of 2024)
laws.status_note: In force.
laws.mechanism: Allows the Central Bank of Kenya to prescribe penalties on institutions, credit reference bureaus and other persons for failure to comply with the Banking Act, prudential guidelines or directions, capped at KSh 20 million or three times the monetary gain made or loss avoided, whichever is higher.
other_mechanisms: Makes consequential amendments to other financial sector statutes listed in the Act.

source.name: Business Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Deletes section 55(2) of the Banking Act and substitutes a new subsection (2): the Central Bank may, in regulations, prescribe penalties payable by institutions, credit reference bureaus or any other person that fails or refuses to comply with the Act, the Prudential Guidelines or any direction issued under them.

Caps those penalties at twenty million shillings for an institution or credit reference bureau, or three times the gross monetary gain made or loss avoided, whichever is higher; three million for a corporate entity and one million for a natural person.
Allows additional penalties of up to one hundred thousand shillings for each day the failure continues.

laws.name: National Rating Act, 2024 (No. 15 of 2024)
laws.status_note: In force.
laws.mechanism: Requires county governments to levy rates on rateable land and buildings under a single national framework for valuation and rating, and creates the National Rating Tribunal, which fixes how an owner's annual rates bill is assessed and challenged.
other_mechanisms: Standardises valuation rolls, valuation notices and objections across counties.

source.name: National Rating Act, 2024, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Part II, Rating: the duty to levy rates. This is the clause that puts a county government under an obligation to rate rateable property.
Establishes the National Rating Tribunal, the forum in which a rating decision is challenged.

laws.name: Excise Duty (Amendment) Act, 2025 (No. 2 of 2025)
laws.status_note: In force; section 1 deems it to have come into operation on 27 December 2024.
laws.mechanism: Deletes the 25 per cent excise duty on imported fully assembled electric transformers and parts, lowering the landed cost of grid transformers for the companies that import them.
other_mechanisms: Rewrites the description of imported float glass for excise purposes.

source.name: Excise Duty (Amendment) Act, 2025, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Amends paragraph 1 of Part 1 of the First Schedule to the Excise Duty Act by deleting the item covering imported electric transformers and parts, at the listed tariff codes, and its corresponding rate of excise duty.

Rewrites the description of imported float glass and surface ground or polished glass for excise purposes, excluding goods of East African Community Partner States that meet the Community's Rules of Origin.
The Act is deemed to have come into operation on 27th December, 2024.

laws.name: Insurance Professionals Act, 2025 (No. 5 of 2025)
laws.status_note: In force.
laws.mechanism: Bars any person from practising as an insurance professional after a twelve month transition unless they hold a current practising certificate, with a fine of up to KSh 50,000 or six months imprisonment for contravention, which changes who may place, underwrite or adjust business for an insurer.
other_mechanisms: Creates the Insurance Institute of Kenya and the Insurance Professionals Examinations Board.
Makes provision for continuing professional development and disciplinary proceedings.

source.name: Insurance Professionals Act, 2025, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: After the expiration of twelve months, or such longer period as the Cabinet Secretary may declare by notice in the Gazette, no person shall practise as an Insurance Professional unless he or she holds a practising certificate that is in force.
Contravention is an offence carrying a fine of up to fifty thousand shillings or imprisonment for up to six months.
Defines what practising as an Insurance Professional is, which is what fixes who the bar in section 41 reaches.

laws.name: Finance Act, 2025 (No. 9 of 2025)
laws.status_note: In force; sections 14 and 62 commenced on 1 January 2026.
laws.mechanism: Adds paragraph 74 to Part I of the First Schedule to the Income Tax Act so that gains on the transfer of securities traded on a securities exchange licensed by the Capital Markets Authority are not chargeable to capital gains tax, which removes the 15 per cent gains charge from trades in listed shares.
other_mechanisms: Cuts the capital gains tax rate to 5 per cent for investments certified by the Nairobi International Financial Centre Authority.
Adds excise duty of 10 per cent on fees charged by virtual asset providers on virtual asset transactions.
Zero rates packaging materials for tea and coffee.
Repeals the digital service tax and insurance premium tax provisions that had been superseded.

source.name: Finance Act, 2025, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Inserts paragraph 74 into Part I of the First Schedule to the Income Tax Act: gains on the transfer of securities traded on any securities exchange licensed by the Capital Markets Authority are not chargeable to tax under section 3(2)(f).
Exempts dividends paid by a company certified by the Nairobi International Financial Centre Authority that reinvests at least two hundred and fifty million shillings in Kenya in that year of income.

laws.name: Capital Markets (Amendment) Act, 2025 (No. 26 of 2025)
laws.status_note: In force.
laws.mechanism: Rewrites section 29 of the Capital Markets Act so that the Cabinet Secretary, in consultation with the Capital Markets Authority, prescribes shareholding limits for each category of licence, replacing the shareholding and governance conditions fixed in the Act itself.
other_mechanisms: Keeps existing licences and approved shareholding structures valid until the new regulations are made.

source.name: Capital Markets (Amendment) Act, 2025, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: The Cabinet Secretary may, in consultation with the Authority, make Regulations prescribing the shareholding limits for different categories of business that require to be licensed or approved under the Act.
Deletes subsections (4), (5), (6) and (7) of section 29 of the Capital Markets Act: the shareholding and governance conditions that were fixed in the Act itself.

Transitional: a licence granted and the shareholding and governance structures approved under it stay valid until regulations made under section 29(3A) come into operation, and the Authority then issues licences in accordance with the limits set in those regulations.

laws.name: Privatisation Act, 2023 (No. 11 of 2023, Cap. 485B)
laws.status_note: Repealed by section 69 of the Privatization Act, 2025 (No. 18 of 2025), which also vested the rights and obligations of the Privatisation Commission in the successor Authority.
laws.mechanism: Created the Privatisation Authority and a statutory procedure for selling government shareholdings in state entities, which was the legal route by which a government stake in a listed company could be offered to the market.
other_mechanisms: Provided for the Privatisation Appeals Tribunal and for privatisation proposals to go to the National Assembly.

source.name: Privatisation Act, 2023, Kenya Law Reports

source_repeal.name: Privatization Act, 2025, section 69, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: The Privatisation Authority.
Methods of privatisation: initial public offer of shares, sale of shares by public tender, sale resulting from the exercise of pre-emptive rights, or such other method determined by the Cabinet.
The privatisation proposal on the entity.
The provision that repealed this Act.

laws.name: Privatization Act, 2025 (No. 18 of 2025)
laws.status_note: In force; it repeals the Privatisation Act, 2023 (Cap. 485B).
laws.mechanism: Sets the permitted methods for selling a government shareholding, including an initial public offer of shares, sale of shares by public tender and sale under pre-emptive rights, each requiring a Privatization Proposal approved by the National Assembly, which is the procedure by which a state stake in a listed issuer can be sold.
other_mechanisms: Establishes the Privatization Authority as successor to the Privatization Commission.

source.name: Privatization Act, 2025, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Methods of privatization: initial public offer of shares, sale of shares by public tender, sale resulting from the exercise of pre-emptive rights, or such other method determined by the Cabinet.
Where an entity has been identified for privatization, the Authority shall prepare a Privatization Proposal on the entity.
Approval of the Privatization Proposal.

laws.name: Government Owned Enterprises Act, 2025 (No. 25 of 2025)
laws.status_note: In force; commenced by Gazette notice on 5 December 2025.
laws.mechanism: Provides for government owned enterprises to be reconstituted as public limited liability companies and for public service obligations to be imposed on them and measured through a performance evaluation regime, which changes the corporate form and the non-commercial obligations of state-controlled issuers.
other_mechanisms: Sets governance, board appointment and reporting requirements for government owned enterprises.

source.name: Government Owned Enterprises Act, 2025, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.cite: Fourth Schedule, paragraph 1(1), made under section 40(2)
clauses.effect: The Government Owned Enterprises listed in the Second Schedule shall, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 30 of the Interpretation and General Provisions Act (Cap. 2), incorporate in their names a public limited liability company under the Companies Act (Cap. 486), and those companies are their successors in rights, duties, assets and liabilities.
Implementation of public service obligations.
Amends the definition of state corporation in section 2 of the State Corporations Act to take in a Government Owned Enterprise established before or after this Act.

laws.name: Provisional Collection of Taxes and Duties (Repeal) Act, 2025 (No. 27 of 2025)
laws.status_note: In force; it repeals the Provisional Collection of Taxes and Duties Act (Cap. 415).
laws.mechanism: Repeals the statute that let the government collect taxes and duties proposed in a Finance Bill before the Bill became law, so a new tax measure now applies only from the date the Act enacting it takes effect.
other_mechanisms: Removes the provisional collection window that previously bridged the period between the budget statement and enactment.

source.name: Provisional Collection of Taxes and Duties (Repeal) Act, 2025, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.instrument: Provisional Collection of Taxes and Duties (Repeal) Act, 2025 (No. 27 of 2025)
clauses.effect: The Provisional Collection of Taxes and Duties Act (Cap. 415) is repealed. That is the whole operative provision: the Act has two sections, a short title and this repeal.

laws.name: Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026 (No. 10 of 2026)
laws.status_note: In force; section 1 deems it to have taken effect on 15 April 2026. The 8 per cent rate runs for 90 days and may be extended once by Gazette notice.
laws.mechanism: Sets value added tax at 8 per cent, instead of the standard rate, on premium motor spirit, illuminating kerosene and automotive gas oil for 90 days, which lowers the tax component of the pump price and of fuel cost for buyers.
other_mechanisms: Allows the Cabinet Secretary to extend the 90 day window by a further 90 days.

source.name: Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Notwithstanding section 5(2), the rate of tax shall be eight per cent of the taxable value for motor spirit (gasoline) premium of tariff number 2710.12.20, illuminating kerosene of tariff number 2710.19.22 and gas oil (automotive, light, amber for high-speed engines) of tariff number 2710.19.31.

clauses.instrument: Value Added Tax Act (Cap. 476), as inserted
clauses.effect: That rate is in effect for ninety days from the date this Act comes into effect, and the Cabinet Secretary may by notice in the Gazette extend it for a further ninety days.

laws.name: Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026 (No. 11 of 2026)
laws.status_note: In force; section 1 brings it into operation on publication.
laws.mechanism: Provides that a transfer of property by a company to its shareholders as part of an internal reorganisation is not a distribution, and adds the same internal reorganisation to the Eighth Schedule exemptions, so a group restructuring does not create a deemed dividend or a capital gains charge.
other_mechanisms: Defines internal reorganisation as a restructuring that does not transfer property to a third party.

source.name: Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) and (b), a transfer of property by a company to its shareholders under paragraph 6(2)(i) of the Eighth Schedule shall not be deemed to be a distribution for the purposes of the Act.

clauses.instrument: Income Tax Act (Cap. 470), Eighth Schedule, as inserted
clauses.effect: Adds the transfer of property by a company to its shareholders in an internal reorganisation to the transactions outside the capital gains charge.

laws.name: Finance Act, 2026 (No. 19 of 2026)
laws.status_note: In force; sections 17, 18 and 24 commence on 1 January 2027 and section 43 on 1 September 2026.
laws.mechanism: Exempts capital gains on the transfer of property to a real estate investment trust registered by the Commissioner, and exempts the instrument conveying that property from stamp duty, removing two transfer taxes from the route by which property moves into a REIT.
other_mechanisms: Halves the Road Maintenance Levy per litre from KSh 3.00 to KSh 1.50.
Raises the collector commission on the Affordable Housing Levy to up to 2 per cent.
Adjusts VAT input tax and credit note rules and changes several excise descriptions.

source.name: Finance Act, 2026, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: Inserts paragraph 76 into Part I of the First Schedule to the Income Tax Act: any capital gains relating to the transfer of property to a real estate investment trust registered by the Commissioner under section 20(1).
Extends the stamp duty exemption to an instrument whose effect is to convey or transfer a beneficial interest in property to a real estate investment trust.
Amends section 3(2) of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund Act (Cap. 427), deleting three shillings and substituting one shilling and fifty cents.

laws.name: Central Bank of Kenya (Amendment) Act, 2026 (No. 23 of 2026)
laws.status_note: In force.
laws.mechanism: Rewrites section 36 of the Central Bank of Kenya Act so the Bank may grant loans and advances to banks and microfinance institutions and give emergency liquidity assistance for up to twelve months, extendable to five years, on collateral it accepts.
other_mechanisms: Allows the Bank to deal in gold and other precious metals.
Extends the Bank's lending to the Kenya Deposit Insurance Corporation to fixed periods not exceeding three years.

source.name: Central Bank of Kenya (Amendment) Act, 2026, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.instrument: Central Bank of Kenya (Amendment) Act, 2026 (No. 23 of 2026)
clauses.effect: Repeals section 36 of the Central Bank of Kenya Act and replaces it: the Bank may, for implementing monetary policy and maintaining orderly market conditions, grant loans or advances to banks and microfinance institutions on terms it determines.

clauses.instrument: Central Bank of Kenya Act (Cap. 491), as replaced
clauses.effect: Emergency liquidity assistance may go to banks or microfinance institutions that meet the Bank's criteria of solvency and viability, are not subject to liquidation, and are assessed as systemically important or likely to cause instability.

clauses.instrument: Central Bank of Kenya Act (Cap. 491), as replaced
clauses.effect: Any such loan or advance is for a period of up to twelve months, which the Bank may extend for a period not exceeding five years.

clauses.instrument: Central Bank of Kenya Act (Cap. 491), as replaced
clauses.effect: All loans or advances under the section shall be secured by collateral acceptable to the Bank, subject to valuation, margin and risk management requirements it determines.

clauses.instrument: Central Bank of Kenya (Amendment) Act, 2026 (No. 23 of 2026)
clauses.effect: Amends section 26(1)(a) of the principal Act by inserting the words and any other precious metals immediately after the word gold.

clauses.instrument: Central Bank of Kenya (Amendment) Act, 2026 (No. 23 of 2026)
clauses.effect: Deletes and replaces section 46A: loans or advances for fixed periods not exceeding three years to the Kenya Deposit Insurance Corporation.

laws.name: Coffee Act, 2026 (No. 8 of 2026)
laws.status_note: In force.
laws.mechanism: Requires the Cabinet Secretary, by Gazette notice, to impose a levy of 2.5 per cent on the export or import value remitted by coffee buyers through the direct settlement system, apportioned between the Institute, the Board, price stabilisation, marketing and coffee growing counties.
other_mechanisms: Restructures licensing of coffee mills, marketers and buyers and provides for a direct settlement system.

source.name: Coffee Act, 2026, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.effect: The Cabinet Secretary shall, in consultation with the Board and county governments and by notice in the Gazette, impose a levy of two point five per centum on the export import value remitted by coffee buyers to the Board through the direct settlement system.

Apportions the levy: thirty per centum to the Institute, fifteen to the Board for regulatory purposes, twenty for price stabilization, ten to the Board for marketing and twenty-five to the coffee growing counties pro rata as a conditional grant.

laws.name: Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021 (Legal Notice 265 of 2021)
laws.status_note: In force; published in Kenya Gazette Vol. CXXIV No. 6 on 14 January 2022 with a six month lead before the registration duty took effect.
laws.mechanism: Requires every data controller and data processor to register with the Data Commissioner and pay the registration fee set out in the Second Schedule, with mandatory registration triggered by listed activities including financial services, telecommunications, property management, health, hospitality, transport, education, gambling and direct marketing.
other_mechanisms: Sets the certificate duration, renewal and refusal grounds, and exempts specified public bodies from the fee.

source.name: Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021, Kenya Law Reports

clauses.instrument: Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021 (Legal Notice 265 of 2021)
clauses.effect: The Regulations provide the procedure for registration of data controllers and data processors under section 18 of the Data Protection Act.

clauses.instrument: Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021
clauses.effect: Subject to regulation 13(1), every data controller and data processor is required to register.

clauses.instrument: Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021
clauses.effect: An application is made in Form DPR1 in the First Schedule and is accompanied by the registration fees specified in the Second Schedule.

clauses.cite: Third Schedule, made under regulation 13(1) and (3)
clauses.instrument: Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021
clauses.effect: The thresholds for mandatory registration: the purposes that oblige registration whatever the size of the controller or processor, among them the provision of financial services, telecommunications, property management including the selling of land, health administration and patient care, hospitality, education, gambling and crime prevention.

laws.name: Finance Bill, 2024 (National Assembly Bill No. 30 of 2024)
laws.status_note: The National Assembly passed the Bill, the President declined assent on 26 June 2024 and referred it back with a recommendation to delete all clauses; the National Assembly Bills Tracker records that no Bill was presented for assent and that the Bill was lost upon deletion of all clauses. No measure in it took effect.
laws.mechanism: Proposed an eco levy on specified goods manufactured in Kenya or imported, alongside a package of VAT and excise changes, which would have added a per unit or per kilogram charge to the cost of the listed goods had it been enacted.
other_mechanisms: The Departmental Committee on Finance and National Planning proposed removing the levy from diapers, tyres, bicycles, wheelchairs and three wheeled vehicles and reducing rates on some finished goods before the Bill was withdrawn.

source.name: National Assembly Bills Tracker, 28 May 2026, Parliament of Kenya

source_secondary.name: Report of the Departmental Committee on Finance and National Planning on the Finance Bill, 2024, Parliament of Kenya

laws.clauses_not_on_file: No clause is named because there is no enacted text to name one in. The Finance Bill, 2024 was withdrawn before enactment, so its provisions never became sections of an Act, and Kenya Law publishes no Akoma Ntoso text for it. The record stands on the Parliament of Kenya sources already cited, and a clause number taken from the Bill as introduced would read as law that was never made.

unresolved: The Social Health Insurance contribution rate of 2.75 per cent is set in regulations gazetted under the Social Health Insurance Act, 2023; the regulations themselves were not opened and are cited here through the Act and through the High Court judgment that records the gazetted rate.

The Alcoholic Drinks Control Act framework that sits alongside excise duty was not amended between 2021 and 2026 in the Acts published by Kenya Law, so no record is carried for it; the excise line is carried through the Finance and Tax Laws amendments instead.

Energy sector tariff setting happens through Energy Act, 2019 instruments and Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority reviews that predate this window; no Act in the 2021 to 2026 list changes the tariff mechanism, so no record is carried for KPLC and KEGN on tariffs.
Competition Authority of Kenya decisions in this window were not verified against an official published determination, so none is carried.
Court challenges to the Finance Act, 2025 and to the Affordable Housing Act, 2024 were not confirmed in an official judgment at the retrieval date, so no in_court status is asserted for them.
